metrics.protocol: Jan–Apr fit, May chooses smoothing by log loss, refit Jan–May, June masked same-basket product retrieval. Alphabetically first drink anchor; order sequence absent. June previously inspected.
metrics.interpretation: Matched GP is the margin of one item already present in the historical basket. It is not incremental profit or recommendation acceptance. Category AUC from earlier work does not transfer to this product-level task.

dollar.interpretation: Smallest whole-cent uniform price step within the enumerated branch-wide policy, or enumerated single-SKU policy with a 5% cap. Not a global optimum across all pricing/discount/mix changes. $1/day is a conditional accounting target, not proven attainable demand response.

substitution.interpretation: Same-category candidates ranked by similarity of historical hourly sales profiles, not an estimated consumer substitution probability. Correlated schedules may share seasonality or popularity. Ingredient groups are editable serving-equivalent assumptions, not verified recipes or allergen data. No automatic transfer of unavailable-product demand.

metrics.lowProfitDefinition: Below branch-specific 20th percentile of Jan 8–Apr 30 recorded daily GP
metrics.alertRule: Calibrated lower GP forecast is below that low-profit threshold; not a probability estimate.
metrics.protocol: Fixed quantile model fit Jan 8–Apr 30. May one-sided calibration. No refit before June; no June tuning. Normal historical conditions only.
metrics.limits: Lower forecast is not a guaranteed floor. Time dependence, shared branches and distribution shift invalidate a simple independent/exchangeable coverage guarantee. It does not predict disruption outcomes.

discount.interpretation: Discount dollars measure fixed-volume financial exposure, not waste or recoverable savings. No recommendation exposure or randomized treatment exists. Larger baskets have more opportunities for a discounted line; no causal lift claim or automatic cancellation is justified.

portfolio.interpretation: Top-three held-out retrieval of GP from products already sold in June. It measures historical profit concentration captured by a ranking, not extra GP caused by promotion. Product forecasts were selected in earlier work; June is an internal holdout. No arbitrary reassignment of demand is modeled.

scenarios.title: Ordinary forecast · constrained resources
scenarios.interpretation: 16 planning and 512 independent evaluation Poisson draws from assumed means. Recorded sales forecasts treated as unconstrained demand; no promotion response or automatic substitution. Stock is integer, terminal salvage zero, no labor/rent/transfer cost, shared serving-equivalent resources are invented and require recipes/inventory validation. Allocation is from a hypothetical shared procurement budget, not measured physical stock transfers.
